title: Multi-Disciplinary Dataset Discovery from Citation-Verified Literature Contexts
text: comprehensive knowledge base of dataset usage patterns [ 18 , 1 ] . We formulate dataset discovery as contextual information extraction over scientific literature. The core idea is to use citation contexts as semantic evidence linking natural-language research questions to datasets. Our system is a three-stage pipeline that combines efficient corpus access with neural extraction and robust entity resolution: (1) scalable citation-context retrieval, (2) neural dataset mention extraction with citation-aware quality signals, and (3) datasets entity resolution for consolidation. This design directly addresses three chronic shortcomings of metadata-only systems: semantic mismatch , contextual ambiguity , and incomplete coverage . Let a research query 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} (free text) and optional field constraints ℱ \mathcal{F} be given. The task is to retrieve and rank dataset entities 𝒟 = { d 1 , … , d n } \mathcal{D}=\{d_{1},\dots,d_{n}\} from a literature corpus. In this work, we operationally define a dataset d d as any named research resource (e.g., corpora, benchmarks, databases) that is explicitly mentioned in a paper as being used, modified, or evaluated against. This definition excludes mentions of software tools or general methodologies. Each entity d i d_{i} is a structured tuple where name i \text{name}_{i} is the canonical identifier, 𝒞 i \mathcal{C}_{i} is the set of supporting citation contexts, and ℳ i \mathcal{M}_{i} contains enriched metadata. We operate on Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) [ 19 ] with a hybrid strategy: precomputed indices for citation windows plus on-demand filtering for query specialization.
